title: Tool calling
lead: A customer asks where their order is. How does the model get current delivery information?

sections.title: Tell the model which tools are available
sections.body:
To look up an order, your application can provide a getOrder tool that takes an orderId.
The model receives the tool’s name, description, and parameter schema. It can then request a call; your application manages the database code and credentials.

sections.title: Model requests, program executes
sections.body:
A user asks: “Where is order A123?”
The model requests getOrder({ orderId: "A123" }).
Node.js validates arguments and authorization, then queries the order.
The application associates the result with the original call and sends it back.
The model turns the result into an answer.

sections.title: Results become context
sections.body:
A tool call does not automatically complete the final answer. Its result enters a subsequent model request, allowing the model to explain the data or request another action.
Message formats, call identifiers, and parallel-call support depend on the model API.

sections.title: Moving on to agents
sections.body:
An application must manage the call loop, dispatch tools, return results, and decide when to stop. A task may call tools several times or answer without using any.
Next, explore how Mastra organizes these steps and which business decisions remain your responsibility.

note: Generated arguments are not automatically trustworthy. Validation, authorization, and controls for side effects belong in the code that executes the tool.
